newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs slide as Nikkei powers ahead.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs slide as Nikkei powers ahead.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures remained weak but off their lows in late Wednesday trade after coming under pressure from surging Tokyo stocks and a weak yen.

Dealers said JGB futures were also hit by talk of cash bond sales by Japanese investors and a vague rumour that another Japanese insurance company with large bond holdings was facing financial difficulties.
News that Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co had been ordered to halt operations caused a sharp sell-off in JGBs last week on fears the company would be forced to liquidate its bond holdings.

The Nikkei's surge past the psychological 19,000 point barrier for the first time since February triggered some institutional selling of Euroyen, but there were no sales of major volume, dealers said.
December Euroyen stood at 98.97 at 1115 GMT after hitting a low of 98.95 against its IMM close at 99.01. Volume was an above-average 16,955 lots.
Dealers said the market was well-bid at December's intra-day low of 98.95 as many doubted the Bank of Japan would raise interest rates soon.
"Some U.S. funds are speculating there will be a rate hike later this year but most in Japan feel the economy still needs a low interest rate environment," a Japanese bank dealer said.
June JGBs ended at 125.05 after falling as low as 124.69 against their previous 125.41.
A trader with a European futures house said they would be supported initially at 125.00 and then at 124.75.
Eurodollar futures ended slightly easier on profit-taking after strong overnight gains in Chicago where U.S. treasuries rallied on a weaker than expected employment cost index and durable goods data.
"The non-farm payrolls are this Friday so people would like to sell the market on any rallies. Most people are looking for at least a quarter percent hike in U.S. rates," the trader said.
December Eurodollars ended at 93.605 against their IMM close at 93.615 on volume of 7,515 lots.
